library(nlmixr2lib)

library(rxode2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ideno_2026_amikacin"))$reference`
* Article: [Ideno 2026, *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol* 15(4):e70235 (open access)](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70235)

Ideno, Kasai and Tanigawara (2026) describe SCOUT (Systematic Covariate
Observational Uncovering Technique): each subject's empirical Bayes estimates
from a covariate-free base model are used to solve for the dose that meets a
therapeutic target, and those individual optimal doses are then plotted against
patient characteristics to decide which covariates to test formally. The method
itself is an estimation device (the dose is written as a bioavailability
parameter `F1 = THETA(1) * EXP(ETA(1))` with a penalised objective function in
NONMEM), not a pharmacometric model, and is not packaged. The paper applies it
to a virtual one-compartment drug (Part 1; a simulation toy, not packaged) and
to two real-drug base models whose estimates are published in the supplement.
Those two models are packaged here:

* `Ideno_2026_amikacin` -- two-compartment IV model with no covariates, fitted
  to the public University of Strathclyde amikacin dataset (Part 2; estimates in
  Data S2).
* `Ideno_2026_eribulin` -- the Majid 2014 three-compartment eribulin PK model
  (typical values fixed) driving an effect compartment and a Friberg
  myelosuppression model with three transit compartments, re-estimated without
  covariates on pooled Japanese phase 2 and post-marketing data (Part 3;
  estimates in Data S3, ODE structure in the Data S1 control stream).

# Population

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ideno_2026_amikacin"))$population)
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ideno_2026_eribulin"))$population)
```

Ideno 2026 does not tabulate demographics for either dataset. The amikacin data
are the adult therapeutic-drug-monitoring records deposited by Thomson et al.
(University of Strathclyde, 2021); Figure 3 shows ages of roughly 18-90 years,
adjusted body weights of 35-93 kg, creatinine clearances of 20-185 mL/min and
both sexes. The eribulin data pool a Japanese phase 2 study (Aogi 2012) with the
Japanese post-marketing survey analysed by Kawamura 2018; Figure 4 shows body
weights of roughly 33-100 kg, baseline neutrophil counts of 1-15 x 10^3/uL,
albumin 1.3-5.0 g/dL, ALP 110-3000 U/L and bilirubin 0.1-2.0 mg/dL.

| eribulin `lke0` | log(0.0203) 1/h | Data S3 table, Keo |

| eribulin `propSd` | 0.360 | Data S3 table, RUV prop |

# Part 2: amikacin

## Closed-form dose check (typical subject)

Ideno 2026 (Methods, Part 2) gives the dose that reaches a target Cmax at the
end of a short infusion of a two-compartment model:

D = Cmax,target * V1 * Dur / [1/ke - (k21 - r1)/(r1 (r2 - r1)) e^(-r1 Dur) - (k21 - r2)/(r2 (r1 - r2)) e^(-r2 Dur)],

where r1 and r2 are the roots of s^2 - (ke + k12 + k21) s + ke k21 = 0. With the
typical values and the paper's target (Cmax 60 mg/L after a 30-min infusion),
the ODE model integrated at that dose must peak at exactly 60 mg/L.

```{r amikacin-closed-form}
# Etas supplied as data columns with omega = NA (common random numbers across
# dose levels) make rxode2 warn "multi-subject simulation without omega"; only
# that warning is muffled.
solve_fixed_eta <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

mod_ami <- readModelDb("Ideno_2026_amikacin")
th_ami <- rxode2::rxode(mod_ami)$theta

amikacin_dose <- function(cl, vc, q, vp, cmax = 60, dur = 0.5) {
  ke <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  b <- ke + k12 + k21
  disc <- sqrt(b^2 - 4 * ke * k21)
  r1 <- (b + disc) / 2
  r2 <- (b - disc) / 2
  den <- 1 / ke -
    (k21 - r1) / (r1 * (r2 - r1)) * exp(-r1 * dur) -
    (k21 - r2) / (r2 * (r1 - r2)) * exp(-r2 * dur)
  cmax * vc * dur / den
}

dose_typ <- amikacin_dose(
  exp(th_ami[["lcl"]]), exp(th_ami[["lvc"]]),
  exp(th_ami[["lq"]]), exp(th_ami[["lvp"]])
)
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_typ, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ami), ev_typ, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
cmax_typ <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 0.5]
c(dose_mg = dose_typ, Cmax_at_end_of_infusion = cmax_typ)
# Same parameters on both sides, so the only difference is integration error.
stopifnot(abs(cmax_typ / 60 - 1) < 1e-6)
```

The typical subject needs about `r round(dose_typ)` mg, which sits at the centre
of the 0.6-2.2 g spread of SCOUT-estimated doses in Ideno 2026 Figure 3.

## Virtual cohort: individual optimal doses

Each simulated subject's own CL, V1, Q and V2 give its own closed-form dose;
re-simulating each subject at that dose confirms the target is met. This is the
analytic shortcut the paper notes (Discussion) for simple compartment models; it
reaches the same optimum as the penalised-OFV estimation.

```{r amikacin-cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_ami <- 150
ev_draw <- rxode2::et(amt = 1000, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(0.5) |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_ami))
draw <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ami, ev_draw, returnType = "data.frame")
indiv <- draw |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0.5) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl, vc, q, vp) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = amikacin_dose(cl, vc, q, vp))

ev_opt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = indiv$id, time = 0, amt = indiv$dose, rate = indiv$dose / 0.5, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  data.frame(id = indiv$id, time = 0.5, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
# Re-use each subject's parameters by supplying the etas as data columns.
eta_cols <- draw |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0.5) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, etalcl = log(cl / exp(th_ami[["lcl"]])),
                   etalvc = log(vc / exp(th_ami[["lvc"]])),
                   etalvp = log(vp / exp(th_ami[["lvp"]])))
ev_opt <- dplyr::left_join(ev_opt, eta_cols, by = "id")
chk <- solve_fixed_eta(mod_ami, ev_opt, omega = NA, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
                       returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0.5)
# Same drawn parameters on both sides of the identity.
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$Cc / 60 - 1)) < 1e-5)
summary(indiv$dose)
```

```{r amikacin-dose-plot, fig.cap = "Individual doses reaching Cmax 60 mg/L after a 30-min infusion, plotted against clearance and central volume (compare the dose spread in Ideno 2026 Figure 3, which plots the same doses against patient characteristics)."}
indiv |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cl, vc), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, dose / 1000)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(cl = "CL (L/h)", vc = "V1 (L)"))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Optimal dose (g)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r amikacin-dose-range}
# Figure 3 places the cohort's SCOUT doses between ~0.6 and ~2.2 g with most
# of the mass around 1.0-1.5 g. The centre is set by the typical V1 and CL and
# does not depend on which subjects land in the tails.
stopifnot(median(indiv$dose) > 1000, median(indiv$dose) < 1500)
```

## PKNCA

Ideno 2026 reports no NCA for amikacin; the table below documents the model's
single-dose exposure for a 1 g, 30-min infusion in the virtual cohort.

```{r amikacin-pknca}
ev_nca <- rxode2::et(amt = 1000, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48)) |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(100))
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ami, ev_nca, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1 g IV over 30 min")
stopifnot(all(sim_nca$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_nca$Cc, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
conc_ami <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_ami <- data.frame(id = seq_len(100), time = 0, amt = 1000, treatment = "1 g IV over 30 min")
nca_ami <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ami, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ami, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
summary(nca_ami)
```

# Part 3: eribulin

## Steady state without drug

The Data S1 initial conditions (progenitor and transit states at BNEU*Kout/Ktr)
put the Friberg chain at steady state, so with no dose the neutrophil count must
stay at baseline.

```{r eribulin-steady-state}
mod_eri <- readModelDb("Ideno_2026_eribulin")
cov_typ <- data.frame(WT = 50, ALB = 39, ALP = 300, TBILI = 0.5 * 17.1, NEUT = 3200)
ev_ss <- rxode2::et(seq(0, 2016, by = 24))
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_eri), ev_ss, params = cov_typ,
                          rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_ss$ANC / 3200 - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

## Typical-patient optimal dose

The SCOUT target in Part 3 is the largest dose that keeps the neutrophil count
at or above 500/uL (no CTCAE grade 4 neutropenia) through four 21-day cycles on
the approved schedule (days 1 and 8 every 21 days) or through the alternate
every-other-week (EOW) schedule, evaluated to 2016 h (Figure S3). Because the
nadir falls monotonically with dose, the penalised-OFV estimate equals the
dose found by bisection.

```{r eribulin-helpers}
schedules <- list(
  "2-week-on, 1-week-off" = c(0, 168, 504, 672, 1008, 1176, 1512, 1680),
  "EOW" = seq(0, 1680, by = 336)
)
bsa_dubois <- function(wt, ht) 0.007184 * wt^0.425 * ht^0.725

eri_events <- function(subj, dose_mgm2, times, obs = seq(0, 2016, by = 4)) {
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = rep(subj$id, each = length(times)),
    time = rep(times, nrow(subj)),
    amt = rep(dose_mgm2 * subj$BSA, each = length(times)),
    evid = 1, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs_rows <- data.frame(
    id = rep(subj$id, each = length(obs)),
    time = rep(obs, nrow(subj)),
    amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "circ"
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subj, -BSA), by = "id")
}

eri_nadir <- function(mod, subj, dose_mgm2, times, ...) {
  sim <- solve_fixed_eta(mod, eri_events(subj, dose_mgm2, times), returnType = "data.frame", ...)
  if (is.null(sim$id)) sim$id <- subj$id[1]
  as.numeric(tapply(sim$ANC, sim$id, min))
}

# Bisection on the log dose scale, run for every subject at once.
eri_optimal_dose <- function(mod, subj, times, n_iter = 22, ...) {
  lo <- rep(0.02, nrow(subj))
  hi <- rep(20, nrow(subj))
  for (i in seq_len(n_iter)) {
    mid <- sqrt(lo * hi)
    ok <- eri_nadir(mod, subj, mid, times, ...) >= 500
    lo[ok] <- mid[ok]
    hi[!ok] <- mid[!ok]
  }
  sqrt(lo * hi)
}

subj_typ <- data.frame(id = 1L, cov_typ, BSA = bsa_dubois(50, 155))
typ_dose <- vapply(schedules, function(tt) eri_optimal_dose(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_eri), subj_typ, tt), numeric(1))
typ_tab <- data.frame(
  regimen = names(schedules),
  typical = typ_dose,
  paper_mean = c(1.26, 1.97),
  paper_sd = c(0.59, 1.00)
)
typ_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (typical / paper_mean - 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Typical-patient optimal dose (mg/m^2 free base)" = typical,
    "Ideno 2026 cohort mean" = paper_mean,
    "Ideno 2026 cohort SD" = paper_sd,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
# Deterministic (typical values, fixed covariates). A mis-transcribed Slope,
# Kprol or Kout moves these by far more than 15%.
stopifnot(abs(typ_dose / c(1.26, 1.97) - 1) < 0.15)
```

The typical patient (50 kg, 155 cm, albumin 3.9 g/dL, ALP 300 U/L, bilirubin
0.5 mg/dL, baseline neutrophils 3200/uL) tolerates about the approved
1.23 mg/m^2 free-base dose on the approved schedule and about 1.6 times more on
the EOW schedule, matching the cohort means in the Results of Ideno 2026.

## Virtual cohort: individual optimal doses (Figure 4)

```{r eribulin-cohort}
n_eri <- 100
set.seed(2026)
lhs <- function(n, sd) sd * stats::qnorm((sample.int(n) - 0.5) / n)
om <- rxode2::rxode(mod_eri)$omega
subj <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_eri),
  WT = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n_eri, 52, 9), 33), 100),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n_eri, 3.8, 0.5), 1.5), 5.0) * 10,
  ALP = exp(stats::rnorm(n_eri, log(300), 0.6)),
  TBILI = exp(stats::rnorm(n_eri, log(0.5), 0.4)) * 17.1,
  NEUT = exp(stats::rnorm(n_eri, log(3200), 0.4))
)
subj$BSA <- bsa_dubois(subj$WT, 155)
for (nm in rownames(om)) subj[[nm]] <- lhs(n_eri, sqrt(om[nm, nm]))

dose_on21 <- eri_optimal_dose(mod_eri, subj, schedules[[1]], omega = NA)
dose_eow <- eri_optimal_dose(mod_eri, subj, schedules[[2]], omega = NA)
res <- dplyr::mutate(subj, `2-week-on, 1-week-off` = dose_on21, EOW = dose_eow)

# The supplied etas are used (not resampled): Kprol must equal its closed form.
chk_eta <- solve_fixed_eta(mod_eri, eri_events(subj, 1, 0, obs = 0), omega = NA,
                           returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_eta$kprol / (0.0570 * exp(subj$etalkprol)) - 1)) < 1e-8)

data.frame(
  regimen = names(schedules),
  sim_mean = c(mean(dose_on21), mean(dose_eow)),
  sim_sd = c(stats::sd(dose_on21), stats::sd(dose_eow)),
  sim_median = c(stats::median(dose_on21), stats::median(dose_eow)),
  paper_mean = c(1.26, 1.97),
  paper_sd = c(0.59, 1.00)
) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Simulated mean (mg/m^2)" = sim_mean,
    "Simulated SD" = sim_sd,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median,
    "Ideno 2026 mean" = paper_mean,
    "Ideno 2026 SD" = paper_sd
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)

c(
  median_ratio_eow_to_approved = stats::median(dose_eow / dose_on21),
  spearman_neut_dose = stats::cor(log(res$NEUT), log(dose_on21), method = "spearman")
)
# Centre, not extremes: the EOW schedule allows a larger dose per
# administration for nearly every subject, and lower baseline neutrophils
# lower the tolerated dose (Ideno 2026 Results and Figure 4).
stopifnot(
  median(dose_eow / dose_on21) > 1.3,
  stats::cor(log(res$NEUT), log(dose_on21), method = "spearman") > 0.2
)
```

```{r eribulin-figure4, fig.cap = "Replicates the layout of Ideno 2026 Figure 4: individual optimal doses against baseline neutrophil count and body weight, for both regimens. Covariates are simulated (see Assumptions), so only the trends, not the individual points, are comparable."}
res |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Baseline neutrophils (10^3/uL)` = NEUT / 1000, `Body weight (kg)` = WT) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`2-week-on, 1-week-off`, EOW), names_to = "regimen", values_to = "dose") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`Baseline neutrophils (10^3/uL)`, `Body weight (kg)`),
                      names_to = "covariate", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(value, dose)) +
  geom_point(shape = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x) +
  facet_grid(regimen ~ covariate, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimated optimal dose (mg/m^2)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r eribulin-figureS7, fig.cap = "Replicates Ideno 2026 Figure S7A: neutrophil profiles on the approved schedule at each subject's optimal dose; every nadir touches the 500/uL line."}
sim_opt <- solve_fixed_eta(
  mod_eri,
  eri_events(subj, dose_on21, schedules[[1]], obs = seq(0, 2016, by = 8)),
  omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame"
)
nadir_opt <- tapply(sim_opt$ANC, sim_opt$id, min)
# Bisection resolution is (log(1000)/2^22) on log dose, so every nadir sits
# within a fraction of a percent of 500/uL (coarser output grid: allow 3%).
stopifnot(abs(stats::median(nadir_opt) / 500 - 1) < 0.03)
ggplot(sim_opt, aes(time, ANC / 1000, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2016, by = 168)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Neutrophil count (10^3/uL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA

Ideno 2026 reports no NCA for eribulin; the table documents the single-dose
plasma exposure of the fixed Majid 2014 PK layer for 1.23 mg/m^2 free base in the
virtual cohort.

```{r eribulin-pknca}
obs_nca <- c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 168)
ev_nca_eri <- eri_events(subj, 1.23, 0, obs = obs_nca) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = ifelse(evid == 0, "central", cmt))
sim_nca_eri <- solve_fixed_eta(mod_eri, ev_nca_eri, omega = NA, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "1.23 mg/m^2 IV")
conc_eri <- sim_nca_eri |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_eri <- data.frame(id = subj$id, time = 0, amt = 1.23 * subj$BSA, treatment = "1.23 mg/m^2 IV")
nca_eri <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_eri, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_eri, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
summary(nca_eri)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **What is packaged.** SCOUT is an estimation procedure; its penalised
  objective function and the dose-as-bioavailability device are not part of the
  models. The Part 1 virtual drug is a simulation toy and is not packaged. The
  amikacin and eribulin base models are packaged as fitted.
* **Eribulin PK layer.** Ideno 2026 states that the Majid 2014
  three-compartment model was "used for the PK component" and reports estimates
  for the PD parameters only (Data S3). The PK typical values and covariate
  equations are therefore taken from Majid 2014 as printed in Kawamura 2018
  section 2.3 (same research group, same post-marketing data) and held fixed.
  Majid 2014 PK between-subject variability is not reported in either source on
  hand, so the PK layer is typical-value only and the eribulin model has no
  residual-error term on plasma concentration.
* **Eribulin units.** The control stream doses micrograms of free base and
  divides by litres, so concentrations are in ng/mL and Slope is in L/ug
  (= mL/ng). The packaged model takes the dose in mg of free base and scales Cc
  by 1000 to the same ng/mL. Neutrophil states are in cells/uL (the source uses
  10^3/uL); the 0.01 x 10^3/uL floor is applied as 10 cells/uL. The proportional
  residual error is unit-free.
* **Eribulin administration.** The Part 3 dataset (Figure S3) carries no RATE
  column, so doses are IV boluses into the central compartment.
* **IIV.** Data S2 and S3 report the IIV and residual terms as standard
  deviations; the packaged variances are their squares. No covariances are
  reported, so the IIV is diagonal.
* **Amikacin cohort.** The packaged amikacin model has no covariates, so the
  virtual cohort only samples IIV. The dose-range check compares the cohort
  median with the spread in Figure 3.
* **Eribulin virtual cohort.** Ideno 2026 publishes no covariate summary. The
  covariates are simulated: body weight normal(52, 9) kg truncated to 33-100 kg,
  albumin normal(3.8, 0.5) g/dL truncated to 1.5-5.0, ALP log-normal (median 300
  U/L, SD 0.6 on the log scale), bilirubin log-normal (median 0.5 mg/dL, SD 0.4),
  baseline neutrophils log-normal (median 3200/uL, SD 0.4; Kawamura 2018 Table 1
  median), and height 155 cm for every subject when computing body surface area
  (DuBois). The ranges are read from the axes of Figure 4. The etas are drawn as
  Latin-hypercube quantiles so every marginal is reproduced exactly.
* **Comparison with the published means.** The paper's 1.26 (0.59) and
  1.97 (1.00) mg/m^2 are means of doses computed from shrunken empirical Bayes
  estimates of real patients (eta shrinkage 22-43% in Data S3); the simulated
  cohort samples the full IIV, so its spread is wider than the paper's, and
  because the dose distribution is right-skewed its mean is pulled up as well
  (the simulated median sits close to the paper's mean). The covariate
  distribution is also simulated, not the paper's. The typical-patient doses are
  the like-for-like comparison and agree within a few percent.
